front_blocks.md: Define **hypothesis**.

back_blocks.md: A **clear, directional and measurable** statement that can be **tested**.

cards.front_md: Define **hypothesis**.
cards.back_md: A **clear, directional and measurable** statement that can be **tested**.

front_blocks.md: What are the three qualities a good hypothesis must have?

front_blocks.md: How many stages are there in the enquiry process?

back_blocks.md: **Six** stages.

cards.front_md: How many stages are there in the enquiry process?
cards.back_md: **Six** stages.

front_blocks.md: The six stages of the enquiry process are planning, methods and data collection, data presentation, **______**, conclusions and evaluation.

back_blocks.md: The six stages of the enquiry process are planning, methods and data collection, data presentation, **analysis**, conclusions and evaluation.

cards.front_md: The six stages of the enquiry process are planning, methods and data collection, data presentation, **______**, conclusions and evaluation.
cards.back_md: The six stages of the enquiry process are planning, methods and data collection, data presentation, **analysis**, conclusions and evaluation.

front_blocks.md: Which model of rivers might a fieldwork hypothesis be based on?

back_blocks.md: **Bradshaw's model**.

cards.front_md: Which model of rivers might a fieldwork hypothesis be based on?
cards.back_md: **Bradshaw's model**.

front_blocks.md: Name one factor that determines the location chosen for fieldwork.

back_blocks.md: The **topic** of the enquiry, **distance**, **accessibility** or **suitability**.

cards.front_md: Name one factor that determines the location chosen for fieldwork.
cards.back_md: The **topic** of the enquiry, **distance**, **accessibility** or **suitability**.

front_blocks.md: The greater the **______** to a fieldwork site, the less time will be available for collecting data.

back_blocks.md: The greater the **distance** to a fieldwork site, the less time will be available for collecting data.

cards.front_md: The greater the **______** to a fieldwork site, the less time will be available for collecting data.
cards.back_md: The greater the **distance** to a fieldwork site, the less time will be available for collecting data.

front_blocks.md: Once the fieldwork location has been decided, what is used to identify the sample sites within it?

back_blocks.md: **Sampling**.

cards.front_md: Once the fieldwork location has been decided, what is used to identify the sample sites within it?
cards.back_md: **Sampling**.

front_blocks.md: Define **risk assessment**.

back_blocks.md: A consideration of **health and safety** in which **hazards are identified**, along with who is at risk and the **precautions** to reduce the risk.

cards.front_md: Define **risk assessment**.
cards.back_md: A consideration of **health and safety** in which **hazards are identified**, along with who is at risk and the **precautions** to reduce the risk.

front_blocks.md: How can the risk of contracting Weil's disease during river fieldwork be managed?

back_blocks.md: **Wash hands** after being in the water, **cover open wounds** and use **anti-bacterial hand wash**.

cards.front_md: How can the risk of contracting Weil's disease during river fieldwork be managed?
cards.back_md: **Wash hands** after being in the water, **cover open wounds** and use **anti-bacterial hand wash**.

front_blocks.md: How can the risk of slipping on rocks during river fieldwork be reduced?

back_blocks.md: Wear **sturdy, appropriate footwear** with **good grips** on the sole.

cards.front_md: How can the risk of slipping on rocks during river fieldwork be reduced?
cards.back_md: Wear **sturdy, appropriate footwear** with **good grips** on the sole.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
A safety helmet should be worn when working below a cliff face.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
You should wear a safety helmet below a cliff face, not climb the cliff, and not work at cliff faces in very wet or windy weather.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

A safety helmet should be worn when working below a cliff face.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

You should wear a safety helmet below a cliff face, not climb the cliff, and not work at cliff faces in very wet or windy weather.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
An aim is a statement that can be tested, while a hypothesis explains what the enquiry is trying to achieve.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
It is the other way round: the **aim** explains what the enquiry is trying to achieve, while the **hypothesis** is the testable statement.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

An aim is a statement that can be tested, while a hypothesis explains what the enquiry is trying to achieve.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

It is the other way round: the **aim** explains what the enquiry is trying to achieve, while the **hypothesis** is the testable statement.

front_blocks.md: Why is sampling used in fieldwork instead of measuring the whole area?

back_blocks.md: There is **not enough time, equipment or access** to measure the whole area being examined.

cards.front_md: Why is sampling used in fieldwork instead of measuring the whole area?
cards.back_md: There is **not enough time, equipment or access** to measure the whole area being examined.

front_blocks.md: Sampling provides a **______** and statistically valid sample of the whole.

back_blocks.md: Sampling provides a **representative** and statistically valid sample of the whole.

cards.front_md: Sampling provides a **______** and statistically valid sample of the whole.
cards.back_md: Sampling provides a **representative** and statistically valid sample of the whole.

front_blocks.md: Name the three main types of sampling.

back_blocks.md: **Random**, **systematic** and **stratified**.

cards.front_md: Name the three main types of sampling.
cards.back_md: **Random**, **systematic** and **stratified**.

front_blocks.md: Define **systematic sampling**.

back_blocks.md: Selecting samples at **regular intervals**, for example every 500 metres or every tenth person.

cards.front_md: Define **systematic sampling**.
cards.back_md: Selecting samples at **regular intervals**, for example every 500 metres or every tenth person.

front_blocks.md: Define **stratified sampling**.

back_blocks.md: Sampling used when the study area includes significantly different parts (**subsets**), so the sample reflects their proportions in the whole population.

cards.front_md: Define **stratified sampling**.
cards.back_md: Sampling used when the study area includes significantly different parts (**subsets**), so the sample reflects their proportions in the whole population.

front_blocks.md: In random sampling, how are the sample points selected?

back_blocks.md: Numbered grid squares over the study area are entered into a **random number generator**.

cards.front_md: In random sampling, how are the sample points selected?
cards.back_md: Numbered grid squares over the study area are entered into a **random number generator**.

front_blocks.md: Which sampling method can be used when a sample site cannot be accessed?

back_blocks.md: **Opportunistic sampling**, using a site as close as possible to the inaccessible one.

cards.front_md: Which sampling method can be used when a sample site cannot be accessed?
cards.back_md: **Opportunistic sampling**, using a site as close as possible to the inaccessible one.

front_blocks.md: Why is random sampling described as the least biased method?

back_blocks.md: **All possible sample sites have an equal chance** of being selected.

cards.front_md: Why is random sampling described as the least biased method?
cards.back_md: **All possible sample sites have an equal chance** of being selected.

front_blocks.md: A disadvantage of systematic sampling is that not all sites have an equal chance of being selected, which increases the **______**.

back_blocks.md: A disadvantage of systematic sampling is that not all sites have an equal chance of being selected, which increases the **bias**.

cards.front_md: A disadvantage of systematic sampling is that not all sites have an equal chance of being selected, which increases the **______**.
cards.back_md: A disadvantage of systematic sampling is that not all sites have an equal chance of being selected, which increases the **bias**.

front_blocks.md: State one advantage of systematic sampling.

back_blocks.md: It is **easy and quick** and covers the **whole study area equally**.

cards.front_md: State one advantage of systematic sampling.
cards.back_md: It is **easy and quick** and covers the **whole study area equally**.

front_blocks.md: What must be known and accurate for stratified sampling to work?

back_blocks.md: The **proportions of the subsets**.

cards.front_md: What must be known and accurate for stratified sampling to work?
cards.back_md: The **proportions of the subsets**.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Random sampling guarantees that the sample fully represents the whole population.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
Representation may be **poor** if the random sites miss large areas, and some selected sites may be inaccessible or unsafe.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Random sampling guarantees that the sample fully represents the whole population.
cards.back_md:
**False.**

Representation may be **poor** if the random sites miss large areas, and some selected sites may be inaccessible or unsafe.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
Stratified sampling can be used alongside systematic and random sampling.

back_blocks.md: **True.**
An advantage of stratified sampling is that it can be combined with systematic and random sampling, allowing comparisons between subsets.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

Stratified sampling can be used alongside systematic and random sampling.
cards.back_md:
**True.**

An advantage of stratified sampling is that it can be combined with systematic and random sampling, allowing comparisons between subsets.

front_blocks.md: Define **analysis** (of fieldwork data).

back_blocks.md: The process which makes sense of data by identifying **patterns, trends, connections and meaning**.

cards.front_md: Define **analysis** (of fieldwork data).
cards.back_md: The process which makes sense of data by identifying **patterns, trends, connections and meaning**.

front_blocks.md: Which type of data is analysed using numerical and statistical methods?

back_blocks.md: **Quantitative** data.

cards.front_md: Which type of data is analysed using numerical and statistical methods?
cards.back_md: **Quantitative** data.

front_blocks.md: Define **mean**.

back_blocks.md: The value found by **adding all the values** in a data set and **dividing by the number of values**.

cards.front_md: Define **mean**.
cards.back_md: The value found by **adding all the values** in a data set and **dividing by the number of values**.

front_blocks.md: Define **median**.

back_blocks.md: The **middle value** of a data set once the numbers are arranged in **rank order**.

cards.front_md: Define **median**.
cards.back_md: The **middle value** of a data set once the numbers are arranged in **rank order**.

front_blocks.md: Define **mode**.

back_blocks.md: The value which occurs **most frequently** in a data set.

cards.front_md: Define **mode**.
cards.back_md: The value which occurs **most frequently** in a data set.

front_blocks.md: What do the mean, median and mode all measure?

back_blocks.md: **Central tendency**.

cards.front_md: What do the mean, median and mode all measure?
cards.back_md: **Central tendency**.

front_blocks.md: Define **range**.

back_blocks.md: A measure of **dispersion**; the distance between the **highest and lowest** value.

cards.front_md: Define **range**.
cards.back_md: A measure of **dispersion**; the distance between the **highest and lowest** value.

front_blocks.md: The **______** range is the part of the range that covers the middle 50% of the data.

back_blocks.md: The **interquartile** range is the part of the range that covers the middle 50% of the data.

cards.front_md: The **______** range is the part of the range that covers the middle 50% of the data.
cards.back_md: The **interquartile** range is the part of the range that covers the middle 50% of the data.

front_blocks.md: Define **anomaly** (in data analysis).

back_blocks.md: A result which **does not fit the pattern or trend** and needs to be described and explained.

cards.front_md: Define **anomaly** (in data analysis).
cards.back_md: A result which **does not fit the pattern or trend** and needs to be described and explained.

front_blocks.md: What kind of analysis is the annotation of photographs and field sketches?

back_blocks.md: A **qualitative** analysis.

cards.front_md: What kind of analysis is the annotation of photographs and field sketches?
cards.back_md: A **qualitative** analysis.

front_blocks.md: What does annotation add to the features shown in a photograph or field sketch?

back_blocks.md: It gives them **meaning** as part of the analysis.

cards.front_md: What does annotation add to the features shown in a photograph or field sketch?
cards.back_md: It gives them **meaning** as part of the analysis.

front_blocks.md: Range is a measure of **______** – the spread of data around the average.

back_blocks.md: Range is a measure of **dispersion** – the spread of data around the average.

cards.front_md: Range is a measure of **______** – the spread of data around the average.
cards.back_md: Range is a measure of **dispersion** – the spread of data around the average.

front_blocks.md: **True or False?**
The median is the value that occurs most often in a data set.

back_blocks.md: **False.**
The **mode** occurs most often; the **median** is the middle value in rank order.

cards.front_md:
**True or False?**

The median is the value that occurs most often in a data set.

**False.**

The **mode** occurs most often; the **median** is the middle value in rank order.

cards.back_md: The **evaluation of data collection**.

front_blocks.md: Name one common limitation of fieldwork data collection.

back_blocks.md: **Accessibility** of sample sites, **sample size**, **duration**, equipment issues or human error.

cards.front_md: Name one common limitation of fieldwork data collection.
cards.back_md: **Accessibility** of sample sites, **sample size**, **duration**, equipment issues or human error.

front_blocks.md: Define **human error** (in data collection).

back_blocks.md: **Mistakes in recording data** or reading the equipment.

cards.front_md: Define **human error** (in data collection).
cards.back_md: **Mistakes in recording data** or reading the equipment.

front_blocks.md: One improvement to data collection is increasing the **______** so that results are more accurate.

back_blocks.md: One improvement to data collection is increasing the **sample size** so that results are more accurate.

cards.front_md: One improvement to data collection is increasing the **______** so that results are more accurate.
cards.back_md: One improvement to data collection is increasing the **sample size** so that results are more accurate.

front_blocks.md: Which piece of equipment would be more accurate than a float for measuring river velocity?

back_blocks.md: A **flow meter**.

cards.front_md: Which piece of equipment would be more accurate than a float for measuring river velocity?
cards.back_md: A **flow meter**.

front_blocks.md: Give one example of an unforeseen issue that could affect fieldwork results on the day.

back_blocks.md: **Road works** or changes in **river flow**.

cards.back_md: **Road works** or changes in **river flow**.

front_blocks.md: When evaluating conclusions, what should the conclusions be checked against?

cards.front_md: When evaluating conclusions, what should the conclusions be checked against?
cards.back_md: Whether they reflect the **aims and hypothesis** set out at the start of the enquiry.

front_blocks.md: Besides increasing sample size, name one other way data collection could be improved.

back_blocks.md: Taking **more measurements** or looking at a **wider range of secondary sources**.

cards.front_md: Besides increasing sample size, name one other way data collection could be improved.
cards.back_md: Taking **more measurements** or looking at a **wider range of secondary sources**.

front_blocks.md: Enquiry evaluation should evaluate how **______** the conclusions were.

back_blocks.md: Enquiry evaluation should evaluate how **reliable** the conclusions were.

cards.back_md: Enquiry evaluation should evaluate how **reliable** the conclusions were.
